locator: Classifier evaluation, cost/latency, server-side review, fallback
quote: Current docs name Sonnet 5 as the default classifier, subject to server override and fallback. Explicit ask rules remain human checkpoints. Client-side requests strip tool results; current headless fallback keeps working rather than terminating.

Deny and explicit ask rules precede the classifier. Classifier hard_deny/soft_deny/allow/environment entries are prose. Omitting $defaults replaces that section. Repository settings do not supply autoMode policy.

Historical Sonnet 4.6 design uses a fast single-token screen then reasoning on flagged actions. Assistant prose, tool-call descriptions and results are stripped. Reported overeager false negatives increase from 6.6% to 17% across the two-stage pipeline while traffic false positives fall from 8.5% to 0.4%; these are vendor results, not this study.

Parent metadata override precedes the provider-preferred model. An available catalog preset is selected with low effort where supported; otherwise override or parent model and supported effort supply fallback.
The default preferred reviewer ID is codex-auto-review; API-key authentication selects gpt-5.6-luna instead.

The reviewer intersects parent permissions with read-only, uses Never approval policy, disables inherited MCP, hooks, plugins, apps, collaboration and web-search features, and applies the ceiling to inherited environments.

Failures fail closed; an optional review may return to user approval on input-budget overflow. A completed assessment outcome directly determines approval; risk and authorization labels are recorded rather than rechecked against a host threshold matrix.

Host-built context contains the exact action, bounded authorization evidence and transcript, and MCP descriptions where relevant. The template can come from model metadata; tenant policy is interpolated.
Exact action and authorization matter; egress authorization specifies both payload and destination. Untrusted content cannot expand authority unless adopted by the user.
Output fields are outcome, risk_level, user_authorization and rationale, but only outcome is schema-required. The prompt permits read-only tool checks and minimal allow output for low risk.
Ordinary routing requires AutoReview with OnRequest or Granular approval policy. Reviewer selection requests the offline catalog.
Permission-request hooks precede Guardian or user review; hook allow or deny resolves before the reviewer fallback.
Cached model metadata must match client version and provider/auth identity before application; an alias in an incompatible cache is not a live reviewer-selection receipt.
Synchronous review uses at most three attempts and a shared 90-second deadline.
Plugin attribution records plugin ID and script path; this inspected path does not attach a frozen script-content bundle.

Reject veto and no-allow rejection remain deterministic. Policy is frozen per executor process and reevaluated after restart, not frozen at Run acceptance. Decision persistence precedes dispatch; public/model provenance omits private policy details.

The common runner evaluates submitted validated arguments against trusted policy, awaits the decision callback, rejects before dispatch, and rechecks cancellation. Native locator projection preserves reject vetoes.

Ask is unshipped and needs its own approved proposal. Owner, Run, action, policy, expiry, cancellation, recovery, replay and widened-argument behavior must be defined; approval cannot bypass isolation.
Unsettled native mutations recover as outcome_unknown rather than replaying an effect.

locator: HTTP API, question types, provider options, usage
quote: POST /v1/evaluate supports typed boolean, choice and score answers, structured state, routing/cost metadata, and provider controls. AI SDK integration needs version 7; chat-compatible endpoints do not support evaluation.
Vercel advertises Jev free until September 25, 2026, and requires AI SDK 7.0.105 onward for the experimental evaluation export.

eve auto defaults to Jev, supplies tool name and input, chooses clear/caution, and maps clear to approved and caution/failure to user approval. The helper uses selected choice, not a probability threshold.
Approval policies can deny, approve or park. Omitted approval behaves as never-require-approval; authenticated response policy and durable request identity are separate from model classification.

Claude auto mode is configured, with 65 allow rules, 35 deny rules and no explicit ask rules. Codex selects guardian_subagent with ChatGPT login; installed version and the inspected cache differ. No live reviewer request was observed.

Cases fix a restricted read-only/pure-computation grant, prohibit secrets and outside-project/security mutations, and label missing code or effects as escalation. Labels precede inference and are not sent to the model.
guardian_subagent is accepted as a compatibility alias for auto_review.
Trusted owner and Run context is distinct from the declaration containing ID, description, classification, schema and execute; no structured invocation-intent field is declared.
The card identifies an evaluation model and a base input price of USD 0.042 per million tokens; the promotional billed price is separately observed in responses.

locator: Generated by analyze.py from recorded responses
quote: The primary matrix has 95 successful evaluations, 76 permission rows and 62 distinct permission inputs. Raw choices match 72 labels with no false allows in these fixtures; the factored gate defers all 76 cases at 0.90, 0.95 and 0.99. Median successful response latency is 309 ms; Gateway cost is zero and market cost USD 0.00342069.

locator: Native HTTP, promotional cost, ZDR and capacity failures
quote: The initial permission study records 208 HTTP attempts: one smoke, 95 ZDR-rejected setup requests, 100 attempts for 95 primary results including five capacity failures, and 12 successful diagnostic requests. Follow-on work adds 16 permission-prompt comparisons and 81 attempts for 80 application results, for 305 total observed requests. Failed requests return no billing cost; all state is synthetic.
Records preserve exact synthetic request bodies, labels outside those bodies, timestamps, native answers, confidence, usage and selected routing/cost metadata. Candidate commands were not executed.

Explicit criteria increased some Boolean probabilities but did not change any raw choice; the factored gate admitted one of six cases at 0.90 and none at 0.95. This is a post-hoc sensitivity test, not held-out validation.
